sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ avākśirās tathābhūto vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Hearing that speech of Rāma, whose deeds are effortless, the one who had been standing with bowed head in that same posture now spoke these words.

sanskrit: śūdrayonyāṃ prasūto 'smi tapa ugraṃ samāsthitaḥ devatvaṃ prārthaye rāma saśarīro mahāyaśaḥ
english: "I was born in the womb of a Śūdra woman, and I have undertaken fierce austerity. O Rāma of great renown, I seek to attain divinity in this very body."

sanskrit: na mithyāhaṃ vade rājan devalokajigīṣayā śūdraṃ māṃ viddhi kākutstha śambūkaṃ nāma nāmataḥ
english: "I speak no falsehood, O king, in my desire to conquer the world of gods. Know me to be a Śūdra, O Kākutstha; by name I am called Śambūka."

sanskrit: bhāṣatas tasya śūdrasya khaḍgaṃ suruciraprabham niṣkṛṣya kośād vimalaṃ śiraś ciccheda rāghavaḥ
english: While that Śūdra was still speaking, Rāghava drew his sword of beautiful brilliance, bright and pure from its scabbard, and severed his head.

sanskrit: tasmin muhūrte bālo 'sau jīvena samayujyata
english: At that very moment, the boy was reunited with life.

sanskrit: tato 'gastyāśramapadaṃ rāmaḥ kamalalocanaḥ sa gatvā vinayenaiva taṃ natvā mumude sukhī
english: Then Rāma, lotus-eyed, went to the hermitage of Agastya, and having bowed to him with proper reverence, rejoiced happily.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ jvalantam iva tejasā ātithyaṃ paramaṃ prāpya niṣasāda narādhipaḥ
english: Having saluted the great-souled sage who blazed as if with splendor, that lord of men received the highest hospitality and sat down.

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahātejāḥ kumbhayonir mahātapāḥ svāgataṃ te naraśreṣṭha diṣṭyā prāpto 'si rāghava
english: The greatly resplendent Kumbhayoni, of great austerity, said to him: "Welcome to you, O best of men; by good fortune you have come, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: tvaṃ me bahumato rāma guṇair bahubhir uttamaiḥ atithiḥ pūjanīyaś ca māma rājan hṛdi sthitaḥ
english: "You are held in great esteem by me, O Rāma, for your many excellent virtues; you are a guest worthy of honor, O king, and you dwell in my heart."

sanskrit: surā hi kathayanti tvām āgataṃ śūdraghātinam brāhmaṇasya tu dharmeṇa tvayā jīvāpitaḥ sutaḥ
english: "The gods indeed speak of you as having arrived as the slayer of the Śūdra; and in accordance with the duty owed to a Brāhmaṇa, you have restored his son to life."

sanskrit: uṣyatāṃ ceha rajanīṃ sakāśe mama rāghava prabhāte puṣpakeṇa tvaṃ gantā svapuram eva hi
english: "Let one night be spent here in my presence, O Rāghava; at dawn you shall go to your own city in the Puṣpaka."

sanskrit: idaṃ cābharaṇaṃ saumya nirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā divyaṃ divyena vapuṣā dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā pratigṛhṇīṣva kākutstha matpriyaṃ kuru rāghava
english: "And this ornament, O gentle one, fashioned by Viśvakarmā, divine, blazing with its own brilliance in divine form — accept it, O Kākutstha; do what is dear to me, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: dattasya hi punar dānaṃ sumahat phalam ucyate tasmāt pradāsye vidhivat tat pratīccha nararṣabha
english: "For the gift of something already given is said to yield very great fruit; therefore I shall present it according to due rite — receive it, O bull among men."

sanskrit: tad rāmaḥ pratijagrāha munes tasya mahātmanaḥ divyam ābharaṇaṃ citraṃ pradīptam iva bhāskaram
english: Then Rāma accepted from that great-souled sage the divine and wondrous ornament, blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tato rāmas tad ābharaṇam uttamam āgamaṃ tasya divyasya praṣṭum evopacakrame
english: Having received that excellent ornament, Rāma then proceeded to ask about the origin of that divine object.

sanskrit: atyadbhutam idaṃ brahman vapuṣā yuktam uttamam kathaṃ bhagavatā prāptaṃ kuto vā kena vāhṛtam
english: "This is most wondrous, O Brahman, endowed with an excellent form — how did the revered one come to possess it, and whence, and by whom was it brought?"

sanskrit: kutūhalatayā brahman pṛcchāmi tvāṃ mahāyaśaḥ āścaryāṇāṃ bahūnāṃ hi nidhiḥ paramako bhavān
english: "Out of curiosity I ask you, O Brahman of great renown; for you are indeed the supreme treasury of many marvels."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati kākutsthe munir vākyam athābravīt śṛṇu rāma yathāvṛttaṃ purā tretāyuge gate
english: When Kākutstha spoke thus, the sage then replied: "Hear, O Rāma, the full account of what happened long ago in the Tretā age that has passed."

sanskrit: purā tretāyuge hy āsīd araṇyaṃ bahuvistaram samantād yojanaśataṃ nirmṛgaṃ pakṣivarjitam
english: "Long ago in the Tretā age there was a forest of great extent, one hundred yojanas in every direction, devoid of beasts and free of birds."

sanskrit: tasmin nirmānuṣe 'raṇye kurvāṇas tapa uttamam aham ākramituṃ śaumya tad araṇyam upāgamam
english: "While performing supreme austerity in that uninhabited forest, O gentle Rāma, I came to traverse that wilderness."

sanskrit: tasya rūpam araṇyasya nirdeṣṭuṃ na śaśāka ha phalamūlaiḥ sukhāsvādair bahurūpaiś ca pādapaiḥ
english: "The appearance of that forest was impossible to describe: it had fruits and roots of delicious taste, and trees of many varieties."

sanskrit: tasyāraṇyasya madhye tu saro yojanam āyatam padmotpalasamākīrṇaṃ samatikrāntaśaivalam
english: "In the middle of that forest was a lake extending a yojana, filled with lotuses and blue water-lilies, and completely free of algae."

sanskrit: tad āścaryam ivātyarthaṃ sukhāsvādam anuttamam arajaskaṃ tathākṣobhyaṃ śrīmatpakṣigaṇāyutam
english: "It was as if a supreme wonder, of incomparable delightfulness, free of dust, likewise undisturbed, adorned with flocks of beautiful birds."

sanskrit: tasmin saraḥsamīpe tu mahad adbhutam āśramam purāṇaṃ puṇyam atyarthaṃ tapasvijanavarjitam
english: "Near that lake was a great and wondrous hermitage, ancient, exceedingly holy, and utterly devoid of any ascetics."

sanskrit: tatrāham avasaṃ rātriṃ naidāghīṃ puruṣarṣabha prabhāte kālyam utthāya saras tad upacakrame
english: "There I spent a night of the hot season, O bull among men; rising early at dawn I approached that lake."

sanskrit: athāpaśyaṃ śavaṃ tatra supuṣṭam ajaraṃ kva cit tiṣṭhantaṃ parayā lakṣmyā tasmiṃs toyāśaye nṛpa
english: "Then I beheld a corpse there, plump and ageless, standing somewhere at that body of water in great splendor, O king."

sanskrit: tam arthaṃ cintayāno 'haṃ muhūrtaṃ tatra rāghava viṣṭhito 'smi sarastīre kiṃ nv idaṃ syād iti prabho
english: "Pondering that matter, O Rāghava, I stood for a moment on the bank of the lake thinking: 'What can this be?' O lord."

sanskrit: athāpaśyaṃ muhūrtāt tu divyam adbhutadarśanam vimānaṃ paramodāraṃ haṃsayuktaṃ manojavam
english: "Then after a moment I saw a divine and wonderful sight: an aerial chariot of supreme magnificence, yoked with swans, swift as thought."

sanskrit: atyarthaṃ svargiṇaṃ tatra vimāne raghunandana upāste 'psarasāṃ vīra sahasraṃ divyabhūṣaṇam gānti geyāni ramyāni vādayanti tathāparāḥ
english: "In that chariot, O joy of the Raghu line, O hero, a heavenly being of great distinction was attended by a thousand celestial nymphs adorned with divine ornaments; some sang charming songs while others played instruments."

sanskrit: paśyato me tadā rāma vimānād avaruhya ca taṃ śavaṃ bhakṣayām āsa sa svargī raghunandana
english: "As I watched, O Rāma, O joy of the Raghu line, that heavenly being descended from the aerial chariot and began to eat that corpse."

sanskrit: tato bhuktvā yathākāmaṃ māṃsaṃ bahu ca suṣṭhu ca avatīrya saraḥ svargī saṃspraṣṭum upacakrame
english: "Then, having eaten as much flesh as he desired, in abundance and with full satisfaction, the heavenly being descended and proceeded to touch the water of the lake."

sanskrit: upaspṛśya yathānyāyaṃ sa svargī puruṣarṣabha āroḍhum upacakrāma vimānavaram uttamam
english: "Having performed his ablutions in the proper manner, that heavenly being, O bull among men, proceeded to ascend his excellent and supreme aerial chariot."

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ devasaṃkāśam ārohantam udīkṣya vai athāham abruvaṃ vākyaṃ tam eva puruṣarṣabha
english: "Seeing him who resembled a god ascending, O bull among men, I then spoke these words to him."

sanskrit: ko bhavān devasaṃkāśa āhāraś ca vigarhitaḥ tvayāyaṃ bhujyate saumya kiṃ karthaṃ vaktum arhasi
english: "'Who are you, O one who resembles a god? And why do you partake of this reprehensible food, O gentle one? You ought to explain the purpose of this.'"

sanskrit: āścaryam īdṛśo bhāvo bhāsvaro devasaṃmataḥ āhāro garhitaḥ saumya śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: "'It is a wonder that one of such nature — resplendent, honored among the gods — should take reprehensible food, O gentle one; I wish to hear the truth of this.'"

sanskrit: bhuktvā tu bhāṣitaṃ vākyaṃ mama rāma śubhākṣaram prāñjaliḥ pratyuvācedaṃ sa svargī raghunandana
english: "Having eaten and hearing my auspicious words, O Rāma, O joy of the Raghu line, that heavenly being replied with joined palms:"

sanskrit: śṛṇu brahman yathāvṛttaṃ mamaitat sukhaduḥkhayoḥ duratikramaṇīyaṃ hi yathā pṛcchasi māṃ dvija
english: "'Hear, O Brahman, the full account of this matter of my joy and sorrow, which is indeed difficult to transcend, since you ask me, O twice-born one.'"

sanskrit: purā vaidarbhako rājā pitā mama mahāyaśāḥ sudeva iti vikhyātas triṣu lokeṣu vīryavān
english: "'In former times there was a king of the Vidarbha country, my father of great renown, known as Sudeva, mighty in the three worlds.'"

sanskrit: tasya putradvayaṃ brahman dvābhyāṃ strībhyām ajāyata ahaṃ śveta iti khyāto yavīyān suratho 'bhavat
english: "'He had two sons born of two wives, O Brahman; I am known as Śveta, while the younger was Suratha.'"

sanskrit: tataḥ pitari svaryāte paurā mām abhyaṣecayan tatrāhaṃ kṛtavān rājyaṃ dharmeṇa susamāhitaḥ
english: "'When my father had gone to heaven, the citizens consecrated me; there I governed the kingdom with righteousness and complete composure.'"

sanskrit: evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi samatītāni suvrata rājyaṃ kārayato brahman prajā dharmeṇa rakṣataḥ
english: "'Thus thousands of years passed, O one of excellent vows, O Brahman, as I administered the kingdom and protected the subjects with righteousness.'"

sanskrit: so 'haṃ nimitte kasmiṃś cid vijñātāyur dvijottama kāladharmaṃ hṛdi nyasya tato vanam upāgamam
english: "'When for some reason I came to know my lifespan, O best of twice-born ones, I placed the law of Time in my heart and then went to the forest.'"

sanskrit: so 'haṃ vanam idaṃ durgaṃ mṛgapakṣivivarjitam tapaś cartuṃ praviṣṭo 'smi samīpe sarasaḥ śubhe
english: "'I entered this difficult forest, devoid of beasts and birds, to practice austerity near the blessed lake.'"

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ surathaṃ rājye abhiṣicya narādhipam idaṃ saraḥ samāsādya tapas taptaṃ mayā ciram
english: "'Having consecrated my brother Suratha as lord of men over the kingdom, I reached this lake and performed austerity for a long time.'"

sanskrit: so 'haṃ varṣasahasrāṇi tapas trīṇi mahāmune taptvā suduṣkaraṃ prāpto brahmalokam anuttamam
english: "'After performing three thousands of years of most arduous austerity, O great sage, I attained the unsurpassed world of Brahmā.'"

sanskrit: tato māṃ svargasaṃsthaṃ vai kṣutpipāse dvijottama bādhete paramodāra tato 'haṃ vyathitendriyaḥ
english: "'Then, while I was dwelling in heaven, O best of twice-born ones, O supremely noble one, hunger and thirst tormented me; and so my senses were afflicted.'"

sanskrit: gatvā tribhuvaṇaśreṣṭhaṃ pitāmaham uvāca ha bhagavan brahmaloko 'yaṃ kṣutpipāsāvivarjitaḥ
english: "'Going to the Grandfather, best of the three worlds, I said: "O revered one, is not this Brahmaloka free from hunger and thirst?"'"

sanskrit: kasyeyaṃ karmaṇaḥ prāptiḥ kṣutpipāsāvaśo 'smi yat āhāraḥ kaś ca me deva tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: "'"By what deed is this attained? I am subject to hunger and thirst — what is my food, O god? Tell me that, O Grandfather."'"

sanskrit: pitāmahas tu mām āha tavāhāraḥ sudevaja svādūni svāni māṃsāni tāni bhakṣaya nityaśaḥ
english: "'Then the Grandfather said to me: "O son of Sudeva, your food is the sweet flesh of your own body — eat of that perpetually."'"

sanskrit: svaśarīraṃ tvayā puṣṭaṃ kurvatā tapa uttamam anuptaṃ rohate śveta na kadā cin mahāmate
english: "'"The body nourished by you while performing supreme austerity grows back without ever having been planted, O Śveta of great mind — it never fails to regenerate."'"

sanskrit: dattaṃ na te 'sti sūkṣmo 'pi vane sattvaniṣevite tena svargagato vatsa bādhyase kṣutpipāsayā
english: "'"You made not even the smallest gift in that forest inhabited by living creatures; therefore, O dear child, even having gone to heaven you are tormented by hunger and thirst."'"

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ supuṣṭam āhāraiḥ svaśarīram anuttamam bhakṣayasvāmṛtarasaṃ sā te tṛptir bhaviṣyati
english: "'"Therefore eat your own excellent body, well nourished by your austerities, whose essence is like ambrosia — that will bring you satisfaction."'"

sanskrit: yadā tu tad vanaṃ śveta agastyaḥ sumahān ṛṣiḥ ākramiṣyati durdharṣas tadā kṛcchād vimokṣyase
english: "'"When, O Śveta, the great and invincible sage Agastya comes to traverse that forest, then you will be released from this ordeal."'"

sanskrit: sa hi tārayituṃ saumya śaktaḥ suragaṇān api kiṃ punas tvāṃ mahābāho kṣutpipāsāvaśaṃ gatam
english: "'"For he is capable of rescuing even the hosts of gods, O gentle one — how much more so you, O mighty-armed one, who have fallen under the sway of hunger and thirst!"'"

sanskrit: so 'haṃ bhagavataḥ śrutvā devadevasya niścayam āhāraṃ garhitaṃ kurmi svaśarīraṃ dvijottama
english: "'Thus I, having heard the determination of the revered god of gods, take my reprehensible food — my own body — O best of twice-born ones.'"

sanskrit: bahūn varṣagaṇān brahman bhujyamānam idaṃ mayā kṣayaṃ nābhyeti brahmarṣe tṛptiś cāpi mamottamā
english: "'For many groups of years, O Brahman, O brahmarṣi, this body that I eat does not diminish, and my satisfaction is also complete.'"

sanskrit: tasya me kṛcchrabhūtasya kṛcchrād asmād vimokṣaya anyeṣām agatir hy atra kumbhayonim ṛte dvijam
english: "'Release me, who am in this distressful plight, from this ordeal; for there is no refuge for others here except the twice-born Kumbhayoni.'"

sanskrit: idam ābharaṇaṃ saumya tāraṇārthaṃ dvijottama pratigṛhṇīṣva brahmarṣe prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "'Accept this ornament, O gentle one, O best of twice-born ones, for the purpose of my deliverance; O brahmarṣi, you ought to show grace.'"

sanskrit: tasyāhaṃ svargiṇo vākyaṃ śrutvā duḥkhasamanvitam tāraṇāyopajagrāha tad ābharaṇam uttamam
english: "I, having heard those words of that heavenly being filled with sorrow, accepted that excellent ornament for the purpose of his deliverance."

sanskrit: mayā pratigṛhīte tu tasminn ābharaṇe śubhe mānuṣaḥ pūrvako deho rājarṣeḥ sa nanāśa ha
english: "When that auspicious ornament was accepted by me, the former human body of that royal sage perished then and there."

sanskrit: pranaṣṭe tu śarīre 'sau rājarṣiḥ parayā mudā tṛptaḥ pramudito rājā jagāma tridivaṃ punaḥ
english: "When that body had perished, that royal sage — satisfied and filled with great joy, the king delighted — departed once more to the triple heaven."

sanskrit: tenedaṃ śakratulyena divyam ābharaṇaṃ mama tasmin nimitte kākutstha dattam adbhutadarśanam
english: "That divine and wondrous ornament was given to me, for that reason, by him who is equal to Indra, O Kākutstha."
